text:
Lina (acct exec): Heads-up - Acme Health risk team pinged asking for: signed subprocessor addendum, an exported redacted dataflow PDF for their vendor intake, CAIQ answers focused on key management + data deletion, and confirmation that trial traffic stays in EU. They want the packet before Tue. Can we turn this around?

Ravi (solutions): We can. Quick Q: do they need full Dedicated or will a hosted EU-only pinning suffice for the trial? Also they asked about encrypted logging vs PII — do we redact inference payloads in logs by default?

Priya (sec eng): Short answers: (1) EU-only pinned hosted = routing + regional pinning but not physically isolated; Dedicated/Private = stronger guarantee (customer VPC options). (2) Logs: inference payloads are redacted at ingestion by default for PHI-sensitive tenants; full payload retention is opt-in and disabled for trials.

Ethan (legal): For a "signed subprocessor addendum" we typically provide the Subprocessor Schedule + DPA signature. If they need a bespoke attestation, Legal needs 48h to review. We can sign the schedule as-is if they accept standard terms.

DeployBot: Subprocessor export available: https://redwood.internal/exports/subprocessors_2026-02-03.csv (redacted). Revision 2026-02-03. :robot_face:

Priya (sec eng): CAIQ snippets I can drop into the packet (pasteable):
```
- AC-17: Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced; mTLS available for private endpoints.
- SC-28: Encryption at rest: AES-256; customer-managed keys supported (BYOK/HSM) for Dedicated and Private.
- IA-2: Identity: SSO (SAML/OIDC) with RBAC; short-lived tokens for inference access.
- AU-6: Logging: request metadata retained 90 days; inference payloads redacted by default for PHI tenants.
- IR-4: Incident response: 24x7 triage; enterprise customers get 72-hour initial RCA for Sev1.
```

Priya (sec eng): Quick ASCII dataflow to include in their intake PDF (redacted vendor names):
```
User (EU) -> Edge (eu) -> Ingest API -> Preprocessor (PII redaction) -> Router -> Inference pool (gpu-eu)
Inference pool -> Cache (redis-eu) [ephemeral]
Model artifacts -> ObjectStore (s3-eu-1)
Audit logs (redacted payloads) -> LogStore (elastic-eu)
Key material: Customer KMS (BYOK) or Redwood KMS (eu)
Telemetry: Metrics -> Datadog (eu) ; Exceptions -> Sentry (eu)
```

Ravi (solutions): Pricing note for the scoping doc: POC expected ~7k req/day, short contexts. Hosted EU-pinning = no license delta, but no BYOK guarantee. Dedicated w/ BYOK & geo pinning = estimate +40% unit uplift for trial (includes reserve GPU). I'll add numbers to the doc.

Lina (acct exec): Good. Action list: (1) Priya - assemble CAIQ + DFD PDF and attach here (2) Ravi - add the pricing appendix (3) Ethan - confirm whether Legal can sign the subprocessor schedule within 48h. I'll send to Acme once we have the pack.

Ethan (legal): Confirmed: I can approve signing the standard subprocessor schedule; bespoke language will take review. ETA 48h for signature on schedule.

Priya (sec eng): Uploading packet now: https://redwood.internal/packets/acme-poc-security-2026-02-03.pdf (redacted). It includes the ASCII DFD, CAIQ snippets, and the redacted subprocessor CSV.

DeployBot: Attached CSV export: https://redwood.internal/exports/subprocessors_2026-02-03.csv (approved for vendor-share).

Lina (acct exec): Sending the packet to Acme now. If they push for an on-prem or air-gapped runbook, tell me and I'll loop Sales Engineering + Solutions.

Ravi (solutions): Thumbs-up. I'll standby for any follow-ups on capacity or test credentials.

Priya (sec eng): :white_check_mark: Packet assembled. If they request longer log retention or different deletion windows, that's an enterprise add-on.

Ethan (legal): :white_check_mark: Subprocessor schedule sign-off in progress.

Lina (acct exec): Closing - thanks all. I'll mark the lead as "Risk pack sent" and update the CRM. :tada:
